subject: MSA / Order Form — inspection window, sampled evidence cadence & pen-test war room
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft sampling approach for ClearPath security exhibit (for legal review)

Kim / Laura — attaching a draft approach to propose to ClearPath for the security exhibit / audit rights section. High-level: instead of full-period raw log handoffs we're proposing a sampled evidence cadence (monthly extracts + two on-demand snapshots per year) and a scoped inspection window for live pen-tests (six business days notice / 48-hour kick window).

Key asks for legal:
- Confirm the language preserves vendor right to redact customer PII in handed extracts (we're proposing a standard redaction clause and hashed identifiers).
- Confirm the suggested inspection window (six business days notice + 48h warm-up) does not trigger additional SLA exposure.
- Flag any obligations that would require on-site access vs. remote evidence delivery.

Attachments: security-exhibit-proposed-sampling-plan.pdf, evidence-sample-list.csv

Thanks — feel free to iterate directly in the PDF comments.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Sowell <alex.sowell@clearpath.health>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Gwen Ito <gwen.ito@clearpath.health>
Date: Wed, 16 Aug 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft sampling approach for ClearPath security exhibit (for legal review)

Vanessa — thanks for the draft. A few clarifying Qs from our security team before we route to procurement: 

1) Sampled extracts: when you say "monthly extracts + two on-demand snapshots" — will each extract include application logs, access logs, and service-config change history? Our Compliance officer needs a short list of retained artifact types.
2) Pen-test window: the proposed 6 business days notice + 48h warm-up is generally workable, but our auditor asks that one weekend be available for a quick follow-up scan. Can that be accommodated?
3) Redaction: we need a bit more specificity — specifically whether we can request masked identifiers (tokenization) rather than hashed strings for reconciliation.

Gwen (cc'd) will own the procurement redlines once security is happy. Happy to jump on a 30-min call — suggested times Thurs AM PT.

— Alex
Head of Security, ClearPath Health
alex.sowell@clearpath.health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Sowell <alex.sowell@clearpath.health>, Gwen Ito <gwen.ito@clearpath.health>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Aug 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft sampling approach for ClearPath security exhibit (for legal review)

Alex / Gwen — appreciate the quick review. Short answers and proposed compromises below; will capture in a redline once we agree on the big items.

1) Extract contents: monthly extracts = access logs (auth events, token lifecycle), request/response metadata (headers, timestamps), configuration change history (control plane events) and a summarized runbook of maintenance windows. We will not include full payload bodies. See attached CSV for sample fields.

2) Pen-test timing: we can add a one-weekend follow-up slot in the calendar, as long as the primary warm-up/coordination remains the first 48 hours of the window. Proposed wording: "Vendor will provide a six business day window with a 48-hour warm-up; at least one weekend day shall be offered during the calendar quarter as an optional follow-up scan."

3) Redaction/tokenization: we can offer tokenization for reconciliation via a reversible tokenization process under an executed DPA addendum, but we need that in writing up front (Covenant and access controls). Otherwise we will provide cryptographic hashes and sample matching keys via secure channel.

Next step: Gwen, if that high-level approach is acceptable I can prepare a legal redline (MSA appendix + Order Form language) and propose a pen-test war room schedule template (2-hour prep + 2-day test block). If you want, we can also loop PenTestOps (our third-party vendor) to scope tooling used.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Gwen Ito <gwen.ito@clearpath.health>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Alex Sowell <alex.sowell@clearpath.health>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft sampling approach for ClearPath security exhibit (for legal review)

Kim / Vanessa — this reads well and the weekend follow-up is helpful. A couple procurement items before legal redline: 
- We need the reversible tokenization approach documented (high-level) — who holds the token mapping and what controls are applied. If Redwood will hold mappings, we need SOC 2 scope confirmation that key management practices meet our standard.
- Please add an explicit clause for "evidence delivery SLA" (48 hours for monthly extracts after request, 10 business days for on-demand snapshots) so our internal audit has measurable deadlines.

If you can include those two pieces in the redline, procurement will run the clause check and we can route to signatures. Thursday 9:30am PT works for a quick call if you want to walk through wording live.

Thanks — Gwen
Director, Procurement & Vendor Risk
ClearPath Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Gwen Ito <gwen.ito@clearpath.health>, Alex Sowell <alex.sowell@clearpath.health>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, PenTestOps <eng@pentestops.io>
Date: Mon, 21 Aug 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft sampling approach for ClearPath security exhibit (for legal review)

Alex / Gwen — thanks for the specifics. Attached is a first-pass redline (MSA Appendix: Security Exhibit) that: 

- Calls out retained artifact types for monthly extracts (access logs, auth events, control-plane change logs, summarized telemetry) and explicitly excludes payload bodies.
- Adds a reversible-tokenization option: Redwood will host token mappings in a KMS-backed key store under SOC 2 coverage; tokenization access requires a signed DPA addendum and a scoped access request.
- Adds the evidence delivery SLA you requested: 48 hours for scheduled monthly extracts (post-request), 10 business days for on-demand snapshots.
- Formalizes the pen-test calendar: 6 business day notice + 48-hour warm-up; one weekend follow-up per quarter; proposed pen-test war room template attached (pen-test-warroom-invite.ics).

Next steps: if that language is acceptable, Kim will upload the redline to DocuSign (link below) and we can kick the procurement review. If you want to run a 30-min call, we have a slot Thurs 09:30 PT.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/clearpath-msa-sign/ZXy7a
Attachments: security-exhibit-proposed-sampling-plan.pdf, evidence-sample-list.csv, pen-test-warroom-invite.ics

— Laura Bennett
Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
